official.description: The Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship Program is a congressionally funded program of the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs, administered by the Institute of International Education since 2001, that provides up to $5,000 in merit-based scholarships to outstanding American undergraduate students with high financial need to pursue credit-bearing academic studies and career-oriented internships abroad. The program aims to develop a generation of future American leaders with the career skills and international networks to advance U.S. national security and economic prosperity, and 72% of Gilman scholars come from small towns or rural communities.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a one-shot, need-weighted award for Pell-eligible U.S. undergraduates heading abroad on a credit-bearing program, so your actual cheque is set by financial need, program length and total program cost, not a flat $5,000. The real gatekeeping step is administrative: both a study abroad advisor and a financial aid advisor at your institution must certify your application, and an application missing either certification is not considered. Build your timeline backwards from the 25 February 2027 student deadline (11:59pm Pacific) so your advisors can certify by 4 March 2027, and confirm your program country sits at Travel Advisory Level 1 or 2 with no Level 3/4 areas on your itinerary. Strong essays linking the specific destination to your career trajectory, plus a concrete follow-on service project plan, carry the application since there is no minimum GPA.
applicant_utility.best_fit: U.S. undergraduate Pell Grant recipients, especially first-time study-abroad students, veterans, and those from underrepresented states or uncommon destinations, who can lock in both advisor certifications before the March 4 advisor deadline.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm Pell Grant receipt now (or documentation that it will disburse during your term abroad) before the cycle opens
Identify and pre-brief both your study abroad and financial aid certifying advisors in January 2027; if your advisor is not registered in the Gilman portal, have them register before the deadline
Match your application to the correct term: the Spring 2027 cycle covers only programs starting 1 May 2027 - 30 April 2028
Check the U.S. State Department Travel Advisory level for your program country and any regions you will visit, and screen your host institution against the Section 1286 NDAA list
Draft the 4 required essays around destination-career fit, adaptability, citizen-diplomacy, and a follow-on service project; no minimum GPA is required, so essays do the differentiating work
Submit days early: the portal locks at 11:59pm PT and no edits are possible after the deadline
common_rejection_risks: Missing one of the two advisor certifications, which alone disqualifies the application regardless of merit
Applying in the wrong term cycle for your program start date
Program country or a sub-region sitting at Travel Advisory Level 3 or 4, or a host institution on the NDAA Section 1286 list
Non-credit-bearing programs, which are ineligible by definition
Lacking proof of Pell Grant receipt for the application period or the term abroad
Generic essays that do not tie the specific program and destination to concrete academic or career outcomes
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The up-to-$5,000 award defrays only part of typical program costs; remaining tuition balance, flights beyond the award amount, personal spending, and pre-departure costs such as passport fees are normally the student's responsibility. The final award is scaled to demonstrated need and program cost, so applicants should plan to cover the gap with institutional aid, loans, or personal funds.

Award amounts are need-determined, so the advertised $5,000 is a ceiling, not a guarantee

Recipients can only hold the Gilman scholarship once; declining previously does not block reapplying if still eligible
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Student submits in the online portal by 25 February 2027, both advisors certify by 4 March 2027, then Gilman screens, panels recommend, the State Department approves, and notifications go out by email in May 2027.

official.description: The Honor Society of Phi Kappa Phi currently awards 40 Fellowships of $8,500 each, six at $15,000 each, and two at $35,000 each to members entering the first year of graduate or professional study. Established in 1932, the Fellowship Program annually provides funding to first-year graduate students pursuing post-baccalaureate degrees across all academic disciplines, and each active chapter may select one candidate from among its local applicants to compete for the Society-wide awards. The Society's award and grant programs together provide more than $1 million annually to members.

applicant_utility.summary: Access, not merit, is the bottleneck here: you can only enter through the local chapter where you were inducted, and that chapter picks exactly one nominee, so contact your chapter officer and lock in their deadline (typically about two weeks before the 15 April 2027 national deadline) as soon as the portal opens on 15 December 2026. Your membership must be current through 15 April 2027, or your initiation completed by 30 June 2027, and you must not have finished 10 or more graduate credits by mid-April. The award is paid straight to you by direct deposit after a Certificate of Registration is filed with the registrar, so plan cash flow around a summer 2027 payout, and note that most of the 48 awards are the $8,500 tier rather than $15,000 or $35,000.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Dues-current Phi Kappa Phi members starting their first full-time graduate or professional programme between May 2027 and February 2028 who can win their chapter's single nomination slot.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm membership status with the national office (800-804-9880) and pay dues early enough to be active through 15 April 2027
If inducted years ago and no longer nearby, apply through the institution where you were inducted, using the online Chapter Directory for the chapter president's email
Ask your chapter officer for their exact deadline and preferred submission method in December 2026, since chapter deadlines vary and are typically two weeks before the national deadline
Verify your graduate credit count stays at 9 or fewer semester hours by the application deadline
Prepare a single-author 2,500-word academic writing sample (or a five-page/five-minute creative sample for arts applicants)

common_rejection_risks: Missing the local chapter deadline, which is usually earlier than the national deadline and is the only one that matters for entry
Letting membership lapse before 15 April 2027, or not completing initiation by 30 June 2027 for invitation-only members
Crossing the 9-hour graduate credit limit, including credits in progress that convert to completed hours before mid-April
Chapter not nominating you because you never made contact or submitted to the chapter at all
Already holding another graduate degree, which breaches the first-graduate-program expectation
Submitting a multi-author or over-length work sample, or work that fails the Society's AI screening
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The fellowship is a one-off cash award, typically $8,500, paid directly to the recipient; tuition, fees, living expenses and relocation costs beyond the award amount, plus graduate programme application fees and any tax liability, remain the recipient's responsibility. Foreign recipients should note the Society may withhold 30% for tax purposes if a W-8 BEN is not properly provided.

applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Portal opens 15 December 2026, you submit the PDF packet to your local chapter by its deadline, the chapter selects one nominee, the national Society judges, and recipients are notified in summer 2027 with funds disbursed after the Certificate of Registration is filed.
